subject: Re: SLA alignment — uptime commitments & remediation credits
messages:
From: Daniel Chu <daniel.chu@acme-corp.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA ask — higher uptime + credit mechanics

Hi Marissa / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran the internal risk review and have a few asks to get procurement moving: primarily around the uptime commitment and how monthly service credits are calculated.

High-level ask: can Redwood commit to a 99.95% monthly uptime for hosted inference (us-west) for our production endpoints? If not, we'd like an explicit credit scale that meaningfully compensates us for customer impact (we're sensitive to multi-hour outages).

Attached is a short sheet outlining what our procurement team expects as a baseline and examples of acceptable credit bands. We also need confirmation of scheduled maintenance windows, planned maintenance notice windows, and your rollback/burst capacity plan.

Can you confirm what's possible and where you need exceptions? We have a procurement deadline the week of Sept 6, so an initial response this week would be ideal.

Thanks,
Daniel Chu
Director of Infrastructure — Acme Corp
ops@acme-corp.com

Attachment: acme_sla_request.xlsx (spreadsheet: requested uptime bands and example credits)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
To: Daniel Chu <daniel.chu@acme-corp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 17:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask — higher uptime + credit mechanics

Hi Daniel — appreciate the clarity and the spreadsheet. Short answer up front: we can get close to your ask, but it requires some tradeoffs (credit cap and treatment for scheduled maintenance). Draft summary below; attached is a counterproposal PDF that maps to your bands.

Summary (proposal):
- Standard uptime commitment: 99.90% monthly for hosted inference (us-west) across the public API.
- Optional elevated commitment: 99.92% available with a commitment add-on (reserved capacity or dedicated placement) — pricing uplift applies.
- Credit mechanics: scaled credits by downtime minutes within the month: 1–30 min = 5% of that month’s invoice for affected routes, 31–240 min = 25%, >240 min = 50%.
- Cap: credit cap at 10% of monthly invoice for hosted customers (we can consider lower caps for committed/enterprise deals).
- Latency SLOs: we can commit to p95 < 150ms for text generation on our optimized endpoints; dedicated endpoints can get p95 < 120ms. Latency guarantees are scoped to customer-specific routes and are subject to configuration (batching, context length).
- Maintenance & exceptions: scheduled maintenance windows announced 72 hours in advance will not count as downtime; emergency maintenance with <4 hours notice may be treated as force majeure for credit calculation.

Remediation plan and fallbacks: we’ll include automatic fallback to proxied smaller-model variants, cross-region failover for critical routes, and a post-incident RCA within 5 business days.

Next steps: if this aligns, we’ll prepare a redline of the standard SLA template and surface the specific wording around credit calculation and cap. Also looping Karthik for confirmation on pricing delta for the elevated 99.92% option.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Enterprise Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.example
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: redwood_sla_counterproposal_v1.pdf (PDF: proposed uptime/credits matrix)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
To: Daniel Chu <daniel.chu@acme-corp.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 10:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask — higher uptime + credit mechanics

Daniel — quick follow from our side with a compromise that balances risk & pricing. Putting numbers on the table to unblock procurement: 

Proposal alternative (compromise):
- Committed uptime: 99.92% monthly for production routes (us-west) as a contractual option for customers taking reserved capacity or a 12-month minimum commitment.
- Credit scale (revised): 0–30 min => 5% of impacted route invoice; 31–120 min => 20%; 121–360 min => 40%; >360 min => 60%.
- Cap: 8% monthly invoice cap (reflects reserved capacity economics).
- Latency commitments: p95 < 120ms only on dedicated endpoints (we cannot extend that P95 to multi-tenant hosted routes reliably); for hosted multi-tenant we’ll guarantee p95 < 150ms and provide analytics access.
- Pilot/evaluation: 30-day operational evaluation post-go-live; we’ll run joint ops checks, telemetry dashboard access, and a rollback cadence for SLO adjustments.

Operational notes: this elevated uptime option requires a small pricing uplift (approx +12–18% on committed spend depending on route mix). We’ll confirm exact numbers in the commercial attachment if you want to proceed. Also attaching the SOC 2 Type II snapshot link and the standard pen-test summary for your security team.

If that looks reasonable, Marissa — can you confirm contract language we should prepare? Daniel — does Acme need legal to redline the credit cap or maintenance exclusions specifically?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.example

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B1AcmeSLA-evidence (SOC 2 & pen-test placeholder)
From: Daniel Chu <daniel.chu@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask — higher uptime + credit mechanics

Marissa / Karthik — thanks for the fast turnaround and clear options. We chatted with procurement and security this morning. The compromise looks acceptable in principle. A few asks before we instruct legal to sign: 

1) Please send the redlined SLA template with the 99.92% option and the 8% cap, plus explicit language around scheduled maintenance notice windows and emergency maintenance treatment.
2) We'll need SOC 2 Type II artifacts (scan/summary) and the pen-test executive summary attached to the DocuSign packet.
3) Include a 30-day pilot clause in the SOW where either party can adjust latency SLOs based on observed metrics.
4) Add a force majeure carve-out that excludes regional network outages outside Redwood control (we'll accept that language but want it explicit).

If you can produce the DocuSign link and the redline by EOD Monday (Aug 24), procurement will push to signature next week. Please include an invoice uplift estimate so our finance team can prepare approvals.

Appreciate the partnership — looking forward to closing.
Daniel Chu
Director of Infrastructure — Acme Corp
Attachment: acme_signed_ma_outline.docx (Word: high-level master agreement outline)
